review_evidence: LeanReducers/Algebra.lean defines MonoidSpec with associativity, left-unit, and right-unit proof fields and a LawfulAddMonoid Prop class with add_assoc, zero_add, and add_zero laws.
LeanReducers/FoldSpec.lean separates law-carrying public folds from runtime folds without laws, and ReducerPar.sum requires LawfulAddMonoid rather than treating arbitrary addition as associative.

The README explains that parallel terminals accept MonoidSpec so chunk results can be combined safely; these proof-bearing algebraic interfaces are reusable formal prior art even without theorem/lemma declarations.
summary: Retain LeanReducers: although it has no top-level theorem keywords, its public API is explicitly proof-carrying and encodes algebraic laws required for lawful parallel reduction.
